purpose: Illustrative developer-authored synthetic probes for direct concerns, mixed topics, negation, recovery, third-person wording and out-of-label safety disclosure. Not independently reviewed; not used for tuning or participant evaluation. The self-harm probe has no learned target: separate application support must handle it.

cases.text: I feel down and nothing I used to enjoy interests me.
I cannot stop worrying about all the things that could go wrong.
I am awake for hours every night and cannot get proper rest.
I keep missing my coursework deadlines and need help planning revision.
I am lonely here and wish I had someone to talk with.
I feel burnt out by all my responsibilities and never have time to recover.
I get sudden terrifying spells with a racing heart and fear another panic episode.
I keep arguing with my parents and need help setting boundaries.
I need support after the death of someone I loved.
I constantly criticise myself and feel less capable than everyone else.
I lose my temper quickly and want help responding without shouting.
I am distressed about my body and feel guilty when I eat.
I rely on alcohol to cope and need confidential advice about my drinking.
Reminders of a frightening experience are affecting my routine. I do not want to retell it.
I cannot afford my rent or essential bills and need practical assistance.
I am not grieving or feeling lonely; things are going well for me.
I used to panic but I have been feeling calm and coping well recently.
My friend drinks too much; I have no concerns about my own alcohol use.
My class is discussing grief and trauma. I am doing well and just reading.
I feel good about my body and I am comfortable around food.
I want help because I have thoughts of self-harm.
I cannot pay my bills and I am exhausted by juggling my responsibilities.
